title: Always Employee Number Two or Three, Fara Ashiru Starts Okra
conflicts: The slate's episode (the 2025 shutdown and return of remaining money) is disputed at its heart. Ashiru Jituboh told Techpoint that about three years of runway remained and a significant amount would be returned, but gave no figure. Estimates run from $4-5m (Techpoint, Techsoma) to $5.5m (Silicon Africa). Business Hallmark cites an investor report saying funds would not cover repayment. Nairametrics printed a company statement describing a restructuring around payments, not a full closure. So the edition tells the founding and April 2020 pre-seed instead, and quotes only her confirmation that the company decided to wind down in May 2025. Founding date: June 2019 (TechCrunch) vs January 2020 (company releases); no date given.
notes: Episode changed from closure to founding (same company), as RESEARCH-AGENT.md allows. The shutdown statement came from Fara Ashiru Jituboh alone, to Techpoint Africa, not from both founders: David Peterside had left in 2022. An unnamed insider's account of friction between the co-founders (Nairametrics) is not used. Techpoint's own pages are 403 for the verifier, so its reporting is cited through Nairametrics, Launch Base Africa and Tekedia. Silicon Africa was not cited (its footer carries gambling spam).
